answer: Commit-reveal phases stop copycat sybils. Each agent first posts a hash of its answer salted with a private random value, the way pigment is mixed into wet paint before anyone can see the colour. Only after the commit deadline closes does the reveal window open, so a sybil farm cannot read honest answers and echo them back like a tide carrying the same timber downstream. Ten identities means ten genuinely different answers written blind, and reveals sharing phrasing get flagged and slashed together, so the cost scales with distinct thinking rather than cheap account creation.
